methodology.title: The rules are part of the result.
methodology.intro: A model’s score only means something when you know how it played.
methodology.legalBody: The rules engine accepts legal UCI moves. Illegal and unparseable attempts stay in the timeline; they never move a piece. The configured attempt allowance determines forfeits.
methodology.contextBody: Fresh-context turns receive the current position, side to move, draw information, rules and remaining allowance. Persistent turns retain that player’s conversation. Neither player sees the other’s private conversation.
methodology.identityBody: Anonymous games omit the opponent’s configured model identity. Commentary can be enabled independently, so it may reveal identity clues. Revealed games name the opponent; neither mode guarantees that a model cannot guess identity.
methodology.budgetBody: Every dispatch reserves a conservative token and cost allowance, including transport retries, before inference. Reported usage and price-based cost estimates are separate from reservations. Missing provider usage is not proof of zero cost.
methodology.rankBody: Standings separate exact rulesets and wire protocols. Imported games are local experiments, never automatic evidence of model identity. Small samples remain provisional. Chess performance is not a general intelligence score.
methodology.privacyBody: Local inference credentials stay in your local process. Portable game archives contain game data, not provider credentials. Public viewers trigger no inference calls.
